items.excerpt: ## Bounded pattern ownership notes ### CDN-Edge Caching An edge can reduce distance and origin work, but only for responses it may reuse. Cacheability is a content and authority contract, not a network location. The cache key, freshness policy and authorization boundary must agree. An authorization header is not a complete design for private edge caching; explicit cache directives can alter reuse rules. A misclassified response can serve one user's private data to another, and a purge can lag the origin. Test the authorization matrix, the purge path and the stale-on-error behavior. items.excerpt: ## 2. Majority quorum arithmetic and the failure envelope In a simplified majority-voting cluster of N eligible voters, a quorum is floor(N/2)+1. A **3-voter** cluster requires 2 votes, and can normally make progress with one unavailable voter if remaining voters can communicate and have necessary log state. A **5-voter** cluster requires 3. Adding an extra voting member can actually increase the quorum without increasing tolerated failures—for example 3 voters → 4 voters raises required votes from 2 to 3. items.excerpt: ## The overload boundary The overload scenario offers 30 requests per second to a 24-request-per-second pool with a 40-request queue and a one-second deadline. The run reports: - success rate 0.6488 (95% CI 0.6443-0.6534); - timeout rate 0.3495 (95% CI 0.3451-0.3540); - rejection rate 0.0005; - mean queue length 12.79; - server utilization 0.9966. The dominant failure is timeout, not rejection. The queue is large enough to absorb arrivals but not large enough to prevent deadline expiry. A report that focuses on rejection alone would miss most of the loss: rejection is 0.05% while timeout is 35.0%.

items.excerpt: ## Engineering pressure A blocking request-per-connection gateway can be simple and effective when each request completes quickly. Persistent downstream connections change the arithmetic: a connection with low activity may still occupy a worker in a blocking implementation, and the load balancer's resource budget becomes tied to waiting rather than useful work. Netflix's existing gateway platform was exposed to growing device and persistent-connection needs. The migration targeted **concurrent connection scalability** and I/O handling, not a universally faster CPU implementation. [src.m9-n07: motivation and "Results of Zuul 2 in Production"].

A safe method is intended not to request a state-changing effect. PUT, DELETE and safe methods are idempotent by their specified semantics. POST has no general automatic-retry guarantee. items.excerpt: ## Why this can look like a lock problem A pinned waiter holds a carrier while it waits. A signaled virtual thread that has been unmounted needs a free carrier before it can run. If every carrier is occupied by pinned waiters, the signaled thread cannot make progress even when the lock itself has been released. An observer may then see a live process, an apparently free lock and no completed requests. That is a scheduler/resource interlock, not necessarily a permanently held mutex.
